proposed.explanation: The evidence provided covers only ETEL's FY2025 and FY2024 consolidated financials. ETEL shows strong fundamental growth: operating revenue rose from 81,677,812,000 EGP to 106,672,946,000 EGP (+30.6%), gross profit grew from 30,492,762,000 EGP to 44,839,110,000 EGP (+47.0%), and net profit more than doubled from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 22,578,063,000 EGP (+123.3%). This supports continuing to hold your existing 100 shares of ETEL over your 5-year horizon. I do not recommend buying additional ETEL shares because your stated goal is to diversify across sectors, and adding to an existing position would increase concentration in a single name. I also cannot recommend selling ETEL; the evidence is positive, not negative. Regarding EFID (500 shares, 10,200 EGP at current price), no financial evidence was provided, so I cannot form a view on whether to hold, sell, or add to that position. Similarly, with no evidence on any other listed company, I cannot recommend a specific new purchase to achieve sector diversification. Your 30,000 EGP cash is best kept as a reserve until you have evidence-based information on a company in a different sector. Risks: ETEL's strong growth is based on a single year-over-year comparison; a one-year jump does not guarantee sustained performance. The construction/engineering sector can be cyclical and sensitive to government spending and macro conditions. Your medium risk tolerance and medium loss-absorption capacity mean you should avoid over-concentrating in any single stock. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
